verdict.summary: Micron is no longer a conventional memory-cycle story: Q3 FY2026 revenue reached $41.46B, GAAP gross margin 84.6% and adjusted free cash flow $18.3B as AI infrastructure tightened high-bandwidth memory and advanced DRAM supply. That operating leverage supports the 70/100 quality score, but it also makes peak-cycle normalization the central contrarian risk. Q4 guidance of $50B revenue and roughly 86% GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin is extraordinary; the valuation therefore embeds scarcity lasting well beyond one quarter. Investors must distinguish those current GAAP margins from mixed-period trailing ratios and must not infer a live entry from the grade. The August 28 quote lacked a captured regular-session opening bar, so the preserved activation remains dormant and the daily structure ends August 27. Wait for valid market-data provenance before using the unchanged entry, stop and targets. Memory pricing, customer inventory digestion, HBM qualification and a large capital-expenditure response can reverse earnings faster than revenue headlines imply.

business.overview:
Micron manufactures DRAM, NAND and related memory products sold through Cloud Memory, Core Data Center, Mobile and Client, and Automotive and Embedded businesses. Revenue is driven by bit shipments, average selling prices, product mix and manufacturing cost per bit. Because fixed fabrication costs are high, modest changes in pricing and utilization create very large swings in gross margin and earnings.

The AI transmission channel runs through high-bandwidth memory attached to accelerators and through server DRAM and data-center SSD content. Q3 FY2026 Cloud Memory revenue of $13.769B and Core Data Center revenue of $11.524B show that AI clusters affect both premium HBM and broader memory demand. Scarcity can lift contract pricing faster than wafers can be qualified and packaged.

What breaks is the cycle. Customers can digest inventory, competitors can add capacity, yields can improve faster than demand, or accelerator architectures can alter memory content. Current 84.6% GAAP gross margin and 80.4% GAAP operating margin are quarter-specific records, not normalized economics. Capital spending, export controls and long qualification cycles can turn today’s shortage into tomorrow’s oversupply before trailing financial statements reveal the change.
business.moat: Micron’s moat is process technology, fabrication scale, yield learning and customer qualification, especially for HBM. It is real but cyclical: Samsung and SK hynix can compete through capacity, product timing and pricing, so scarcity is not permanent pricing power.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Micron's Q3 FY2026 filing reconciles 1.128B basic weighted-average shares to 1.145B diluted shares through 17M employee-equity-plan equivalents; excluded anti-dilutive shares were not material for the quarter. The 1.145B quarterly diluted average is the minimum observable denominator, while a current point-in-time fully diluted count remains unavailable because the cover share count and all unvested awards are not combined into one current total. At the $923.17 quote, that minimum implies about $1.057T equity value and $1.037T enterprise value after $6.38B debt and $26.02B cash. No reviewed 2026 filing establishes an ATM or equity sale.

filings.finding: The Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q supports $41.456B revenue, 84.6% GAAP gross margin and $7.1B capital expenditure, and reconciles 1.128B basic weighted-average shares to 1.145B diluted through 17M employee-plan equivalents; excluded anti-dilutive shares were not material.

The FY2025 Form 10-K establishes the audited memory-cycle, fabrication, customer, export-control and capital-intensity baseline against which the extraordinary fiscal 2026 HBM-driven margin expansion must be evaluated.

The August 26 Form 8-K appoints Manish Bhatia as President and COO and Scott DeBoer as President and Chief Technology and Products Officer, while Sumit Sadana transitions to Senior Advisor; it contains no financing or securities sale.
